### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 32907ae9ce0f020a966c5363eaca2a688240e47a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fdb5c086d0a29f4d53ad4670503a5d35fe3da417` — the merge of head `40b7e036b8dc409d7312448bf3a8d39bbc4382f5` into base `32907ae9ce0f020a966c5363eaca2a688240e47a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fdb5c086d0a29f4d53ad4670503a5d35fe3da417 && git checkout fdb5c086d0a29f4d53ad4670503a5d35fe3da417
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 32907ae9ce0f020a966c5363eaca2a688240e47a 40b7e036b8dc409d7312448bf3a8d39bbc4382f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 32907ae9ce0f020a966c5363eaca2a688240e47a && git merge --no-ff 40b7e036b8dc409d7312448bf3a8d39bbc4382f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 32907ae9ce0f020a966c5363eaca2a688240e47a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 32907ae9ce0f020a966c5363eaca2a688240e47a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3ffa21c9de78aee8ddd86b0bce888d7af84ead6d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/operator-object-write-value.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.select-shape.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-data-select-shape.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES`, `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES`, `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES`, `isMultiValueField`, `valueSchemaFor`), packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`SelectOptionSchema.value`, `multiple`), packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts (`invalid_value_shape`, `invalid_type_array`), packages/core/src/utils/multi-value-storage-form.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (write-door ordering, 16400–16428), packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts (unique enforced at the driver). Not reviewed: `.changeset/29244-select-object-array-value.md` (prose face, read for ②).

Inputs: card #29244 (body, triage 6575520401, claims 6582080861 / 6582152970, dev report 6584899923), ruling #29346 B (6579813296), PR #29540 body, file list and net diff at the head, and the head's check-runs. The published spec and the cited code were read on `origin/main`, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change the diff implies, read against the cited code on `main`:

1. **Single-value `select` / `radio`, no `options`: a plain object or an array is refused `invalid_type` (sentence `invalid_value_shape`, detail "expected one option value, received an object / an array").** RIGHT. On `main` the arm (`record-validator.ts` 1689–1710) returns `null` when `allowed.length === 0`, before reading the value, so both shapes reached `driver.create` / `driver.update` as sent; the card measured that at `45e9b2f1`, the dev re-measured at `04e0c2c0`. The spec's stored element for an option field authored without `options` is `z.string()` (`field-value.zod.ts` 716–719), never an object or an array.
2. **Single-value `select` / `radio` WITH `options`: `['a']` is refused `invalid_type`.** RIGHT. On `main` membership is judged by `String(value)`, and `String(['a']) === 'a'`, so the array passed and the driver stored `['a']`. The spec's element is `z.enum(codes)`; an array is not a member.
3. **Single-value `select` WITH `options`: a plain object moves from `invalid_option` to `invalid_type`.** RIGHT. On `main` the refusal was an accident of `String({a:1}) === '[object Object]'` failing membership (the #5922 header says exactly this about the four accidental cells). A shape refusal ahead of a membership refusal is the string arm's #29133 order and the operator rule's own order; the wire code `invalid_type` is ADR-0114 vocabulary already in use. Named in the changeset.
4. **Shape test runs ahead of `shapeOnly`, so a `readonly` select's value is judged under `'include'` / `'only'`.** RIGHT. #21663's `ReadonlyValueScope` is "a readonly field's VALUE is still judged for its SHAPE", and the #29133 string arm sits in the same position. On `main` a readonly free select returned `null` before any shape question.
5. **Shape test runs ahead of `picklistUnresolved()`.** RIGHT by construction: a picklist-bound select that received an array gets the shape sentence instead of "list did not resolve"; neither admits the write, and the shape is the earlier fact.
6. **The #5922 operator rule still runs first and keeps its sentence.** RIGHT. The operator check (1193–1240 on `main`) precedes every per-type arm and is untouched; the new test `a filter-operator object keeps its own, earlier sentence` and the two restated pins assert it.
7. **Multi-value option branch (`multiple: true` select/radio, `multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags`): an element that is a plain object or an array is refused `invalid_type` (detail "expected an array of option values, received an element that is …").** RIGHT. On `main` (1714–1748) the branch admitted any array when `allowed.length === 0` and judged each element by `String(v)` otherwise, so `[['a']]` passed membership as `'a'`. `valueSchemaFor` derives `z.array(element)` with `element` a string or an enum member (752). The rule sits inside `if (!isValueShapeJudgedType(t))`, so multi-valued `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image` stay on the ADR-0104 arm; no second shape rule for them (the #22908 ban holds).
8. **A non-array on a multi-value field keeps `invalid_type_array`; a lone scalar is still wrapped.** RIGHT. `multiValueStorageForm` (core) wraps string / number / boolean and leaves an object untouched; the element rule is reached only after `Array.isArray(value)`.
9. **No new error code, no new catalog sentence, no `packages/spec` change.** RIGHT. `fail('invalid_type', { type, detail }, 'invalid_value_shape')` is the exact call the string arm (1278) and the ADR-0104 arm (1789) make; the four-locale catalog entry exists on `main`.
10. **Public surface.** No export, type or signature moves in `@objectstack/objectql`; `validateRecord` / `validateRecordInScope` keep their shapes. The narrowed face is a data write's answer, served by every door that runs the record validator (engine insert / insertMany / update by id / update by predicate / `validate()`; REST POST / PATCH; flow record nodes; screen-flow resume). The two #5922 pins the card ordered re-homed are restated as refusals asserting the shape sentence and the absence of "filter operator" in the message, which is what they proved before (the operator rule did not claim `{ $inn }` or `{ a: 1 }`); moving them to `json` would pin nothing because `valueMayBeAnObject` skips the operator rule for `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`.
11. **Unique collision.** Unchanged in kind, moved in time: `unique` is enforced at the driver (`memory-driver.ts` 438–444; SQL as a translated driver error, `engine.ts` 16428 / 16504), and `validateRecordInScope` runs at 16402 before `driver.create`, so an object or array on a `unique` free select is now refused 400 before any 201 / 409 could be answered. A string pair still answers 201 then 409. No stored row is rewritten or re-judged.
12. **Filters.** Not touched by this diff; the filter door already refuses an object or array comparand on a select (`engine-nested-object-door.test.ts` on `main`). The write door now agrees with the read door.

Not implied by the diff, and correctly left alone (see ③ OQ2): a number or boolean on a single-value select, and a number or boolean element on a multi-option field, are still admitted and stored as sent.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29244-select-object-array-value.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, title `fix(objectql)!: …`, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, a BREAKING banner with FROM → TO and the one-line caller fix, the one code move named. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. Per AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3 a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition; this is the exact shape of the landed precedent `.changeset/29133-text-field-refuses-object-array.md`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value or metadata type an author writes moves; `SelectOptionSchema.value` and `FieldSchema.multiple` are untouched. The `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` check-runs on the head are `success`. The level matches what the diff publishes.

`Clause-②:` no (narrowing) — matches the card's `Level` line, the claim's expectation, and the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry, answered:

**OQ1 — scope wider than the card (declared-options select refusing `['a']`; object on a declared select moving `invalid_option` → `invalid_type`; the element rule on `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` as well as `multiple: true` select). Dev recommends A, keep.** ANSWERED: A, keep, with the three parts tested one by one against the spec on `main`:
- *Does any published spec declare that a single-value select accepts an array?* No. `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` is documented "value is one declared option code"; `valueSchemaFor` returns `element` (not `z.array`) unless `isMultiValueField`, and `element` is `z.enum(codes)` or `z.string()`. `['a']` was admitted by `String(['a'])`, which is the #5922 header's "accident, not a rule". Refusing it makes the spec's own stored shape real; it takes no declared capability away.
- *Does any published spec declare that `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` accept object elements?* No. `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` is documented "value is an array of option codes (tags: free-form)"; `valueSchemaFor` comments "tags (and option types authored without options) are free-form strings" and derives `z.array(z.string())` / `z.array(z.enum(...))`. The branch on `main` is one branch for all five types (`isMultiValueField` is true for the three inherently-multi types and for `multiple: true` select/radio); a per-type split would leave the same line admitting the same shape on its siblings, which is the one-definition drift #17469 / #18408 closed.
- *Does the `invalid_option` → `invalid_type` move take anything away?* No. Both are refusals of the same write; the code moves from an accidental membership failure to the shape sentence that names what is wrong. ADR-0114 `invalid_type` is already the code every shape refusal carries. The changeset names the move.
- *Unique-collision behaviour:* see ① 11 — the refusal now precedes the unique check; no new admission, no new 409.
- Census: the dev's log-only probe found 0 product writers across objectql, rest, runtime, service-automation and the dogfood battery, 2 test writers (the two pins). I did not re-run it (read-only); the head's check-runs are the gate for suites the probe did not cover.

**OQ2 — a number on a single-value select is still stored as a number though the spec's element is `z.string()`. Dev recommends a follow-up card.** ANSWERED: A, file the card; out of this card's scope (the card names objects and arrays). Three things belong on that card, all read in the tree, none a defect this PR introduces: (i) a number or boolean on a single-value select is admitted by its string reading and stored raw (the #29241 text-family normalisation is the precedent, and it moved a `unique` answer, so it is its own narrowing); (ii) a number or boolean ELEMENT on a multi-option field is admitted the same way; (iii) `isPlainObjectValue` is deliberately prototype-strict (a `Date`, a `Map`, a class instance are "not a plain object"), so such a value on a free select still falls to membership and is stored as sent — the string arm has the same posture by the same helper, so this is the family's question, not this arm's. The new control `expect(errorsOf({ free: 3 })).toEqual([])` pins (i) as present behaviour; the follow-up card will move that pin.

**Dev flag — landing hold behind #29464 (ruling #29346 B, execution step 3).** ANSWERED, holds: #29464 is open, not merged, `draft: false` at my read, head `22a77935`; its file list touches `record-validator.ts` (`normalizeBlankTypedValues`) and this diff does not touch that function, the blank/`''` arm or the `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` arm. This PR's `mergeable_state` is `blocked` as expected. The seat sequences; the record does not lift the hold.

**Dev flag — AGENTS.md section 10 pre-PR `origin/main` merge deferred.** ANSWERED: ordered by the card delta; `origin/main` moved to `390bd2ae` with no commit on the five files and a clean `merge-tree` per the report. The re-run on the merged head is owed before landing, as the PR body says. Not a review finding.

**Dev flag — census built with `OS_SKIP_DTS=1`, 6 TS7016 reds in the census leg only.** ANSWERED: a build-mode artifact of a probe worktree, restored and removed; the head battery on a full-declaration build is green and CI type-checks the head. Not a finding.

**Dev flag — PR assignee / reviewer not set; PR activity not subscribed.** ANSWERED: both are the standard order's own posture. Not findings.

**Out-of-scope finding (carrier: none).** The number-on-select item is OQ2's card. Nothing else was carried.

No flag is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself, judged against the published spec on `main` and the cited code, with every attempt to break it named:

**What the spec declares.** ADR-0104 D1's value contract (`field-value.zod.ts`) is the one authority for an option field's stored shape: `select ⇒ option code` in the module header; `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` "value is one declared option code"; `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` "value is an array of option codes"; `valueSchemaFor` derives `z.enum(codes)` or `z.string()` per element and `z.array(element)` only when `isMultiValueField`. `SelectOptionSchema.value` is a `SystemIdentifierSchema` string. Nowhere does the spec declare an object or an array as a single select's stored value, or an object or a nested array as a multi-option element. **The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the write door; it takes no declared capability away at the consumer.** It is the select arm's instance of the #29133 string-arm rule, with the same helper (`isPlainObjectValue`), the same posture (never silently alter a value), the same code and the same catalog sentence.

**Attempts to break it:**

1. *Is `select`-without-`options` a declared "free-form" capability that admits anything?* No: `valueSchemaFor` makes it `z.string()`, not `z.unknown()`; the module says openness is an explicit decision and reserves `z.unknown()` for `json` and the computed types. A free select is a free STRING, as the spec reads it.
2. *Does the single-value test misfire on a `multiple: true` select?* No: the gate is `!isMultiValueField(def)`, the spec's own predicate (#18408), so a multi select falls to the array branch, where the element rule applies.
3. *Does the element rule reach multi-valued `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image` and create a second shape rule (#22908 ban)?* No: it sits inside `if (!isValueShapeJudgedType(t))`, so those types still parse under `shapeSchemaFor` on the ADR-0104 arm with its posture flags.
4. *Does it run under `shapeOnly` before the readonly strip and change a value's identity?* No: it mutates nothing; it only refuses. `normalizeMultiValueFields` still does the only payload write, before validation, and only wraps scalars.
5. *Does it collide with #29464's blank arm?* No overlap in the tree: `normalizeBlankTypedValues` and the `''` path are not touched; `isMissing(value)` returns before this arm for `''`, `null`, `undefined`.
6. *Does the operator rule lose its sentence?* No: it runs first (`!valueMayBeAnObject(def)` is true for a single select) and returns before this arm; `{ $in: [...] }` on a free select still says "is a filter operator, not a value".
7. *Does the enforcement posture differ from the ADR-0104 arm's warn-first?* Yes, deliberately and by precedent: the #29133 string arm and the #20309 number arm enforce unconditionally; warn-first is the reference / structured-JSON class's evidence-gated posture, not the scalar classes'. The census found no product writer, and the ablations prove each half of the rule is load-bearing.
8. *Can a declared-options select be hurt by `['a']` being refused where a UI might send a one-element array?* The spec gives no such write form; `Metadata-protocol` and the authoring form (`object.form.ts`) author a single select's value as one code; the dev's census found 0 such writers in the UI-driving dogfood battery. A remaining caller is told exactly what to send by the sentence and the changeset.
9. *Does anything about a stored object/array row change on read?* No: rows are not rewritten or re-judged, and `os migrate value-shapes` does not scan option fields; the changeset says so.

**Findings.**

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix (none blocks):
- S1. `record-validator.select-shape.test.ts`, `what the rule leaves alone`: `expect(errorsOf({ free: 3 })).toEqual([])` pins the number admission the dev names as a spec gap (OQ2). Mark the pin as "present behaviour, OQ2's card" in its comment, or restate it as "not judged by THIS rule", so the follow-up card inherits a pin it is meant to move rather than one that reads as a contract.
- S2. OQ2's follow-up card should name all three siblings read in ③ OQ2 (number / boolean on a single select, number / boolean element on a multi-option field, a non-plain object such as `Date` or `Map` on a free select via `isPlainObjectValue`), so the normalisation lands once for the option family as #29241 did for the text family.
- S3. The header comment of `record-validator.ts` ("Rules applied (in order…)") now mentions the select shape rule under `select / multiselect`; the numbered rule list in that header still lists `operator object` first and the string arm's #29133 shape rule is not listed there either. Cosmetic; align when the OQ2 card touches the file.

**Verdict grounds.** Every accept-set change the diff implies is the spec's stored shape made real at the write door (①); the changeset level and declarations match the diff and the precedent (②); every flag and open question is answered, none escalated (③); the narrowing takes no declared capability away and survives each probe above (④). The head's check-runs: see the line below.

Check-runs on `3ffa21c9`: all 48 check-runs completed (35 `success`, 13 `skipped`), read at 2026-11-02T18:41Z; none concluded `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`. The gate families this diff derives are `success`: Build Core, Test Core (8 shards), Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint · ESLint and the scoped lint gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI and Live E2E UI. The UI build / lint / type-check matrix, Temporal Conformance and the opt-in harnesses are `skipped` by the path filter (no `ui/` or driver path in the diff). Their conclusions are the gate verdicts this record adopts.
